title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops & Top Support Issues
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This page consolidates the developer-experience (DevEx) documentation standards, canonical quickstarts and templates, API example patterns, docs site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. Intended audience: SDK maintainers, DevEx engineers, technical writers, and on-call support engineers.

Goals
- Provide a single, well-maintained reference for all public SDK and quickstart content.
- Reduce triage time by documenting canonical fixes for top support issues.
- Standardize the docs site publishing and rollback workflow to reduce broken examples.

Ownership and SLAs
- Owner team: engineering (DevEx)
- Content owner: Ava Martinez (DevEx Docs)
- Reviewers: see metadata list above
- SLA for doc updates: critical fixes - 8 business hours; non-critical content updates - 5 business days.

Standards & Conventions
- Language: English (US). Use complete sentences and remove first-person references.
- Tone: engineering-friendly, concise, action-oriented.
- File naming: short, descriptive, dashed lowercase (e.g. developer-sdk-python-quickstart-2026.json).
- Code examples: include at least one curl and one language SDK (Python or JavaScript) for each API surface.
- Snippets must be runnable: keep secrets and API keys as placeholders (API_KEY_HERE).

Sections in this doc
1) SDK guides: structure and expectations
2) Quickstarts & templates catalog
3) API examples: canonical patterns
4) Docs site operating procedures (publishing, CI, rollback)
5) Top support issues and canonical fixes

1) SDK guides: structure and expectations
- Each SDK guide must include:
  - Short intro and intended audience
  - Install instructions (pip/npm/yarn)
  - Authentication and env var setup
  - Minimal example (sync and streaming where applicable)
  - Error handling and retry guidance
  - Reference links to API docs and changelog

SDK release cadence and versioning
- Major releases: breaking changes, 3 months notice in changelog and docs.
- Patch releases: bugfixes and doc updates can be published with tags.
- Semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) required for all SDKs.

Required metadata for each SDK guide (add as a front-matter block in the source repo)
| key | example |
|-----|---------|
| language | python |
| package_name | redwood-sdk |
| sdk_version | 0.14.2 |
| last_tested | 2026-01-28 |

2) Quickstarts & templates catalog
- Quickstart types we maintain:
  - Minimal text generation (Python + curl)
  - Chat app (Node.js + streaming)
  - Embeddings search (Python + SQLite example)
  - Reranking pipeline (Go + HTTP example)
  - Private deployment example (VPC connector + configuration)

Canonical template layout (repo or docs repo)
- /quickstarts/<name>/README.md (overview + run instructions)
- /quickstarts/<name>/examples/<lang>/ (runnable example)
- /quickstarts/<name>/Dockerfile or terraform/ if infra required
- metadata.json (name, description, languages, last_updated)

Example quickstart metadata table
| field | required | format |
|-------|----------|--------|
| name | yes | dash-case string |
| description | yes | short sentence |
| languages | yes | list (python, node, go) |
| run_command | yes | shell command |

3) API examples: canonical patterns
- For each API surface provide: curl, Python (requests & sdk), JS (fetch or sdk) and streaming example where appropriate.

Text generation (curl)
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer API_KEY_HERE\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Write a short haiku about latency."}'
```

Python (sdk)
```
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood(api_key=\"API_KEY_HERE\")
resp = client.generate(model=\"redwood-1-small\", input=\"Write a short haiku about latency.\")
print(resp.text)
```

Streaming (JS)
```
import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
const stream = await client.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-1-small', input: 'Long-form summary...' })
for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk) }
```

Function/tool calling pattern
- Provide typed schema for tool inputs and explicit example of how the SDK maps function calls to the runtime.

Embeddings + similarity search (Python)
- Show batching example, upsert, index maintenance, and a minimal similarity query.

4) Docs site operating procedures
Publishing workflow
1. Author creates a feature branch in docs repo.
2. Add/modify page with front-matter metadata and examples.
3. Open a PR and assign at least two reviewers (1 DevEx engineer + 1 tech writer).
4. CI runs: lint + link-check + run.Examples smoke tests (see tests/docs-smoke/).
5. After approvals, merge to main. CircleCI pipeline deploys to staging site automatically.
6. QA in staging: verify examples run and rendering is correct.
7. Promote to production via the docs deploy job.

CI checks (must pass before merge)
- markdownlint (no broken headings)
- link-checker (no 4xx/5xx links)
- code-snippet-runner (runs lightweight examples against sandbox keys)
- accessibility check (axe-core)

Publishing checklist (author to confirm in PR description)
- [ ] Examples run with sandbox keys
- [ ] No hard-coded secrets
- [ ] Metadata populated
- [ ] Reviewer sign-off

Rollback procedure
1. If a production docs deploy breaks examples or introduces security exposure, open an emergency PR reverting the merge commit.
2. Tag the PR with #docs-emergency and alert #devex on Slack.
3. CI will deploy the revert; confirm staging and production.
4. Postmortem required for any outage >1 hour.

5) Top support issues and canonical fixes
This section lists recurring support tickets and step-by-step canonical fixes that on-call and support engineers should follow. Each item includes: symptom, quick triage, root cause patterns, canonical fix, tests to validate, and postmortem tags if required.

Issue A: SDK auth failures (most common)
- Symptom: 401 Unauthorized from SDK calls; curl with same key succeeds.
- Quick triage:
  1) Verify environment variable set (REDWOOD_API_KEY) in process.
  2) Check SDK version (older SDKs had different header name).
  3) Inspect request headers in logs for missing Authorization header.
- Root cause patterns: old SDK pinned to deprecated auth header; environment not exported in service user context; secrets rotation without config update.
- Canonical fix: upgrade SDK to >=0.12.0 and ensure service account env vars use secrets manager. Example systemd unit snippet:
```
[Service]
Environment=REDWOOD_API_KEY=/run/secrets/redwood_api_key
ExecStart=/usr/bin/my-service
```
- Validation: SDK request logs show 200; run `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY'` matches SDK response.

Issue B: Streaming responses stall after initial tokens
- Symptom: First chunk is received then no further data; client-side reads hang.
- Quick triage: check network proxies (NGINX) and timeouts; verify client uses chunked transfer decoding.
- Root cause patterns: reverse-proxy buffering, incorrect Transfer-Encoding, or client not consuming asynchronously.
- Canonical fix: ensure upstream proxy has chunked transfer enabled and disable response buffering: (example nginx config)
```
location /v1/ {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection \"\";
}
```
- Validation: end-to-end streaming example should deliver tokens continuously for 30s test.

Issue C: Embeddings mismatch or degraded search quality
- Symptom: Similarity results suddenly less relevant after a deploy.
- Quick triage: confirm embedding model id and dimensionality; check index schema and normalization settings.
- Root cause patterns: model changed (unintended version pin), index rebuild not performed, or quantization profile applied incorrectly.
- Canonical fix: pin embedding model in config, run full index rebuild with recorded seed, and validate with canonical query set.
- Validation: canonical eval set recall@10 within 2% of baseline.

Issue D: Examples fail due to rate-limiting in sandbox environment
- Symptom: 429 responses from sandbox keys while examples expect higher throughput.
- Quick triage: look at X-RateLimit-* headers, confirm request volume.
- Canonical fix: add exponential backoff with jitter to examples and include a note in quickstarts about sandbox rate limits.
- Code snippet (python retry)
```
import time, random
for attempt in range(5):
  resp = client.generate(...)
  if resp.status_code == 429:
    time.sleep((2 ** attempt) + random.random())
    continue
  break
```

Issue E: Docs CI failing because code-snippet-runner cannot reach external services
- Symptom: CI job times out on docs-smoke tests.
- Quick triage: check network egress rules for CI workers; verify sandbox API endpoints.
- Canonical fix: ensure CI has access to docs-sandbox region or run offline mocks for the snippets. Add fallbacks in the test harness.
- Validation: CI green for docs-smoke with mocked responses.

Operational playbook: triage steps for new recurring issues
1. Create a short doc under confluence/eng-developer-experience/known-issues when a new pattern appears.
2. Add canonical fix and automated test to docs repo.
3. Assign owner and remediation ETA.
4. Notify #support and #devex with remediation plan.

Appendix: Useful commands
- Run doc lint locally: `npm run docs:lint`
- Run snippet tests: `pytest tests/docs-smoke/`
- Publish local build to staging: `./scripts/deploy-docs --staging`

Contact and escalation

- Pager: DevEx on-call (see oncall rota)
- Slack channels: #devex, #docs, #support
